title: How Muppets Work
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss how the Muppets work and the history of Jim Henson's puppet characters. They cover Henson's early local Washington D.C. show Sam and Friends, early puppets like Kermit, the Sesame Street and Saturday Night Live years, the launch of The Muppet Show, and the performers who voiced and puppeteered key characters, including Frank Oz. Behind-the-scenes segments explain how Muppets are built (foam, Muppet fleece, the Henson stitch, pupil size), hand-and-rod and live-hand operation, right-handing, full-body characters like Big Bird, platforming, forced perspective, and the background "whatnot" Muppets. The episode closes with Muppet spinoffs and films, Henson's death, and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and Rainbow Connection
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with a Rainbow Connection reference and announce the episode is about how the Muppets work, with a brief disclaimer for people who don't want behind-the-scenes details.

segments.title: Jim Henson's early puppets and Sam and Friends
segments.summary: Henson's early work at a Washington, D.C. TV station with Sam and Friends, an adult satirical show that introduced Kermit. Early puppets such as Yorick and Harry the Hipster are mentioned, along with Jane Nabel (later Jane Henson) and Frank Oz joining the team, and Rolf the Dog's origin in Purina dog food commercials.

segments.title: Road to The Muppet Show
segments.summary: Muppets appear on Ed Sullivan and other shows. ABC pilots fall through, Sesame Street launches, and the early SNL sketches with larger muppets fail because writers did not write for puppets. Henson then secures a deal with ITC and CBS, and the pilot called Sex and Violence leads to The Muppet Show.

segments.title: Muppet performers and voices
segments.summary: The hosts discuss which characters Henson voiced (Kermit, Rolf, Waldorf, Dr. Teeth, Ernie) and Frank Oz's roles (Bert, Grover, Miss Piggy, Fozzy, Yoda). They note Oz's later directing and acting career.

segments.title: Building Muppets: materials, eyes and stitching
segments.summary: Henson moved from paper mache to foam, settling on reticulated polyurethane foam. Kermit's original skin was made from a green coat of Henson's mother and his eyes from a toy. Pupil size signals a muppet's age, and pupils are placed closer together. Don Sahlin created the Henson stitch, and the fabric is called Muppet fleece.

segments.title: Hand-and-rod, live-hand and right-handing
segments.summary: Explains hand-and-rod puppets operated with one hand inside the head and rods for the hands, live-hand puppets like the Swedish Chef, and right-handing where a second performer operates one hand, as Frank Oz did for Rolf and Ernie. Most puppeteers are right-handed, so most Muppets are left-handed.

segments.title: Full-body Muppets, platforming and forced perspective
segments.summary: Covers full-body characters like Big Bird, operated with a stretched performer and a wire linking the arms. Also covers platforming, trenches, the underwater shot for Kermit on the log in the Muppet Movie, muppet switching, the car-driving stunt, monitors worn on performers' chests, and forced perspective for sets. Carol Burnett's comment on acting with Kermit is noted.

segments.title: Whatnots, Muppet films, spinoffs and Jim Henson's death
segments.summary: Discusses background Muppets called whatnots, Miss Piggy's costume designer, Kermit's trench coat on Sesame Street, the Thirty Rock comparison, the Muppet films, Fraggle Rock, Muppet Babies, Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas, a Muppet stage show, and Jim Henson's death from a bacterial infection.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode with a song snippet and a sign-off directing listeners to howstuffworks.com.
